chapter_name: Employment: Growth, Informalisation and Other Issues
learning_objective: 🎯 Analyze India's workforce composition, the phenomenon of jobless growth, the shift toward the informal sector, and different types of unemployment.

key_vocabulary.definition: All persons who are working (employed) PLUS those who are not working but are actively seeking work (unemployed).
Only those persons who are actually engaged in economically productive activities.
The increasing proportion of the workforce moving into the unorganized/informal sector lacking social security benefits.
The process where the workforce increasingly shifts from regular salaried jobs to casual wage labor.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: This ratio shows the proportion of the population actively contributing to the production of goods and services. It is higher in rural areas because poverty forces people (including children and the elderly) to take up any work, whereas urban people often study longer or wait for better jobs.

The Formal (Organized) sector includes government and large private companies (10+ workers) offering regular salaries, pensions, and maternity benefits. The Informal (Unorganized) sector includes small shops, street vendors, and farmers. Over 90% of India's workforce is trapped in the informal sector without any social security.

During the late 1990s and 2000s, India's GDP grew rapidly due to the IT and Services boom. However, this growth was driven by advanced technology, not by hiring massive amounts of labor. Thus, we produced more output without creating matching employment—called Jobless Growth.

1) Disguised Unemployment: Common in agriculture; 5 people are working on a farm where only 3 are needed. The marginal productivity of the extra 2 is zero. 2) Seasonal Unemployment: Farm workers sit idle for months after harvesting. 3) Frictional: Time gap when switching jobs. 4) Structural: Mismatch between skills taught and skills the market demands.

fun_activity.title: 🔍 The Disguised Worker Game
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine it takes 3 students exactly 1 hour to decorate the classroom blackboard. If 2 more friends join to 'help', but the blackboard still takes exactly 1 hour to decorate because there isn't enough space for everyone to paint, those 2 extra friends are 'Disguisedly Unemployed'! They look busy, but add zero extra output.

exam_tips: 📌 To calculate Unemployment Rate: (Number of Unemployed ÷ Total Labour Force) × 100. Remember, the denominator is Labour Force, NOT total population.
📌 Self-employment is the major source of livelihood for both men and women in India, followed by casual wage labor.
📌 Mention MGNREGA (Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act) as a key government initiative providing 100 days of guaranteed wage employment to rural households.
quick_recap: ⭐ The majority of India's workforce still resides in rural areas and is primarily dependent on agriculture.
⭐ Women form a larger proportion of the workforce in rural areas compared to urban areas.
⭐ The transition of workers from the primary sector (agriculture) to secondary and tertiary sectors is moving very slowly in India.
